## Cumulative guards (in-sample)

| Guards added | Wrong caught | Neutral caught | Rights killed | Uniform 50: still firing (wrong) | ≥ EUR 100 m band, 229: still firing (wrong) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0: the 15 zero-cost features | 41 | 0 | 0 | 46 (5) | 192 (59) |
| + same winners + same title | 47 | 0 | 2 | 44 (3) | 186 (55) |
| + multi-supplier rule (Σ-bids) | 68 | 4 | 12 | 43 (2) | 152 (35) |
| + TED re-key test | 77 | 9 | 16 | 41 (1) | 136 (27) |
| + top award ≥ 100 × next | 81 | 10 | 17 | 41 (1) | 130 (23) |
| + identical figure on two lots | 86 | 10 | 18 | 41 (1) | 124 (18) |

That still leaves the band about 15 % wrong (18 of 124). The 19 remaining wrongs all need a fact the API lacks: the stated total's provenance, `TED-LOT_NO`, BT-710/711, or lot text.

The biggest single fix is to store a notice's stated total (II.1.7 / BT-161 / BT-27-Procedure / BT-118) as a procedure figure instead of collapsing it into an award copy. By the readers' notes, 73 of the 105 wrongs had such a total; 72 of the 160 rights did too, and there it mostly equals the sum.

The labels disagree on Swiss multi-winner per-lot sums: 7 right, 4 neutral, 12 wrong, and no API field separates them. Any guard on that shape trades about 10 rights for about 20 wrongs; refusing all of them is the fail-closed choice.

## What any guard must keep (right shapes)

- **One winner per lot**: 99 of 160 rights have a single winner on every summed lot. 101 rights have the same contractor on two or more lots, so "same contractor holds 2+ summed lots" must never be used alone.
- **Per-lot award notices**: 42 rights, each notice awarding one lot.
- **Modification-only chains**: 25 rights, each notice restating its own distinct lot.
- **UK FTS frameworks with one value per lot on TEN-k-0**: 9 rights, up to 8831876 at GBP 26 bn, which also has a dominant lot (63 % of S) and an identical pair (L1 = L7).
- **Single-supplier frameworks where BT-709 = BT-720**: BT-709 is sometimes copied onto every lot (37368, 312399, 467379, 964877).
- **Multi-winner shares that sum to the lot's own BT-709/BT-660** (329035, 360576, 738630), or shares of clearly different sizes (1117130, 750775).
- **TED multi-lot award notices whose `LOT-k` matches LOT_NO k**, including integer multiples (8426318).
- **Legitimately dominant lots**: 8831876, 1037353, 839942.
- **Sums equal to the notice's stated total**: this is the positive signal.

Path W's existing guards miss these shapes for specific reasons:
- G1' ignores repeats below 1/10 of the largest lot.
- G3 never includes a lot's own superseded award.
- G4 needs a ratio strictly above 10× (6956639 is exactly 10×, 136136 is 9.8×).
- G8b reads only the key's spelling, so LOT-0000/0001 and LOT-0001/0002 re-keys pass.

feats.schema: The file is a JSON list of 70 rows, sorted by id; money is in integer cents with a currency. Requested fields: id; label{verdict,class,group}; procedure_type, taken from the tender detail or, when the detail has none, from the notice's BT-105; is_framework, true/false/null (from BT-765/766, the eForms-DE ContractingSystem code, TED-*FRAMEWORK*, or a dps classification; null for 14 tenders, mostly eForms modification notices without BT-765, plus the FTS tenders and one F25); stated_total{cents,currency,field,kind,notice_id,notice_valued_lot_results} or null. stated_total prefers the notice that awards the most valued lots, so check notice_valued_lot_results before treating it as a procedure total: 1 means a single-lot notice's BT-161, which is that lot's figure. lots[{key, published_lot_no, estimate_cents, currency, awards[{notice_id, contractor_names, contractor_ids, cents, currency, decision, notice_result}]}]. Extras on each lot: key_number (canonical.rs lot_number), published_lot_no_norm/_src, key_matches_published, lot_no_by_notice, estimate_src (the API keyed estimate first, else the notice's TED-VAL_OBJECT / BT-27-Lot, else the result's TED-VAL_ESTIMATED_TOTAL), lot_amounts, bids, and summed. notice_result inside an award carries the result block's TED-LOT_NO/ITEM/title and amounts, including BT-709/660/710/711 and TED LOW/HIGH. summed_lots is path W's set: per lot, the latest award by notice id, above 10.00, not a sentinel, in currency K. Each summed lot also has lot_section_lot_no versus result_lot_no and result_item, with result_lot_no_matches_lot_section, which flags the ITEM/LOT_NO collision. sum_cents and max_lot_award_cents follow. Other extras: stated_totals (every amount found, with kind), lotnull_amounts (tender-scope figures stored in the detail, provenance unknown), notices_read{src,scheme,form}, served_value_at_fetch, and rebuilt_sum_equals_served, which is true on all 70: every head still served lot-sum-awards when fetched. How the data was read: all 70 details were fetched fresh at 2.5 s spacing. /v1/lots was not fetched, because it returns the same records as the detail's lot_details. Notice content was read for each summed lot's notice plus the newest award notice, 151 notices: 74 fetched fresh, 77 taken from copies the earlier reads saved under v551. There were no errors and no 408s. TED LOT-k is a per-notice ordinal, so key_matches_published being false is not an error by itself: several right-labelled TED tenders have it false on every lot. Scripts: d551w/p0scripts/extract.py, common.py and fetch.sh.

The file is a JSON list with one object for each of the 70 ids at index%4==1, read fresh today: 70 GET /v1/tenders/{id} and 311 GET /v1/notices/{nid}/content (one more was already fetched by a probe). Every notice-level amount is also kept in stated_totals with a scope, and scope 'single_lot_notice' marks a per-lot award notice's own total. Each object also has lots [{key, kind, title, published_lot_no (raw TED-LOT_NO, BT-137 or DE1 lot id from the newest notice that describes the key, else the key's spelling), published_lot_no_norm, published_lot_nos_by_notice, published_lot_no_varies (the same key carries different published numbers across notices: a TED re-key), published_lot_no_differs_from_key, title_lot_no, estimate_cents, currency, estimate_source (the API's keyed estimated_value, else a TED notice's VAL_OBJECT or V.2.3 figure), lot_amounts, awards [{notice_id, result_key, contractor_names, contractor_ids, cents, currency, decision, published_lot_no from that award's own notice, summed_by_w, the notice's lot_division / n_lot_sections / lots_awarded, bt709/bt660/bt710/bt711/ted_initial_estimate from the notice when present, bids}]}]. scored:
I wrote and ran the scorer. None of the guard sets you asked for (A to E, their combinations, or Z) is fit to adopt. The strongest set I found is W13, a sharpened mix of B, C, D and E plus four extra checks. On the 279 labels it refuses 103 of 105 wrongs and costs 54 of 160 fixes. In the uniform 50 it ships 32 heads with 0 wrong, so about 9,825 of the 15,352 fires would remain. All of this is in-sample, and it is not ready to adopt.

**How it was scored.** I re-ran the part-3 extractor over all 279 ids so every id has the same facts from every version notice. That needed 114 notice fetches, with no 408s and no errors. It reproduces `features_part2.json` and `features_part3.json` exactly, and the rebuilt sum equals the served `lot-sum-awards` value on all 279. 8 long chains were read on a bounded set of notices (oldest two, newest, all cached): 327861, 489596, 511903, 531641, 794186, 5571139, 8259278, 8401934.

The wrong rate counts wrongs among the heads still shipped. Bounds are two-sided exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95 %. "Fires left" is 15,352 × (sample heads shipped / 50).

**What W13 refuses** (any one check is enough):
- **Bm_g:** a lot won by 2 or more separate tenders. A consortium on one tender, or a TED result flagged AWARDED_TO_GROUP, counts as one. With no tender rows it refuses.
- **C_plus:** published LOT_NOs collide, are a list, a key's award notices name different lots, or a LOT_NO is missing in a set summed from several notices.
- **D_keys:** a notice's award total (BT-161, VAL_TOTAL, BT-118 or BT-1118, excluding a single-lot notice's own award) is below the summed lots that notice awards, ×1.01. With no total, the sum exceeds 10× every estimate.
- **E.**
- **The shapes pass's 15 zero-cost API features.**
- **C_title:** same winners and same lot title on two keys from different notices.
- **P10:** an award is ≥10× or ≤1/10 of the same key's earlier award.
- **DOM10:** the largest award is ≥10× the second.

W9 is the same set with A and without DOM10.

**Recommendation.** Take W13, with W12 as the stricter fallback, to a fresh uniform 30 and a fresh band read before adopting anything.
- **Why not W12:** adding A catches one more band wrong (27915) but costs 33 more fixes. Among them are unit 2's own pins, the Lyon-Turin trio and 8426318.
- **The bar is met only in-sample:**
  - The 15 API features were picked on these same labels. C_title, P10, DOM10 and the consortium exception in Bm_g were added after I read the first candidates' leftover wrongs.
  - 0 wrong in 32 still allows up to 11 %. At that rate a fresh 30 passes "≤1 wrong" only 15 % of the time.
  - "0 farther" holds by label class only. The reader of 51385, labelled a slip (both lots ×1000), says it is farther than the old figure. W13 still ships it and 27915 (one multi-lot contract counted per lot). No exposed fact detects either.
- **Building it needs facts LotSums does not carry today:** winners per lot result, which tender each winner is on, TED AWARDED_TO_GROUP, published LOT_NO, each total tied to its notice, and lot titles. Storing the stated procedure total as a procedure figure is still the biggest single fix.

**The 4,745 records.** `merge_rule.serve` reproduces unit 2's 6 path-W fires: 585917, 5995030, 6450467/69/73 and 8426318. Unit 1's export has no contractors, framework flags, LOT_NOs or notice totals. So I fetched the 2 fires not in the 279, plus unit 2's 4 holdout fires, with 6 tender reads and 16 notices, and ran the same extractor.
- W13 keeps all 6 of the 4,745's fires, all read right. W12 and W9 keep only 5995030.
- Across all 10 out-of-sample fires, W13 ships 8, all right. It refuses 7256284 (right) and 5977060 (closer).
- These records are the value band plus unit 1's R group, not a uniform sample. The 15,352 projection above therefore comes from the uniform 50.

judge.decision:
REDESIGN path W as "v2", but measure it before any Rust is built. The Rust switch LOT_SUM_AWARDS_PATH stays false until a fresh sample passes the bar.

v2 is today's T', K and G0–G8b plus ten refusal families, R1–R10. One of them, R10, requires a total the buyer stated whenever the sum is EUR 100 m or more.

How it is tested: a salted shadow walk over the failed drain's 15,352 path-W corrections, scored with the Python port of v2, gives the fresh uniform 30. The band heads v2 still ships (15 in-sample) are re-read in full. Only on a pass do the build units B1–B5 run.

A fallback is fixed in advance. "Vouched everywhere" is v2 with R10 applied at every size. It is tested once, from the same walk, only if v2 fails. If it fails too, path W stays withdrawn for good and 551 closes on path V.

Neither the shapes pass's W13 nor W12 is adopted as scored. On these same labels W13 ships 27915 (a double count) and 51385 (two x1000 slips; its reader calls the sum farther) in the EUR 100 m band. The band set is fixed, so a fresh band read would see both again and fail. W12 still ships 51385.
judge.rule:
PATH W v2 (`lot-sum-awards`). It runs only where path V does not fire, as today.

KEPT UNCHANGED (canonical.rs awards_lot_sum, store already has the inputs): T', K, G0, G5, G5', G6, G7, G8, G8b, G1', G2, G3, G4.

NEW REFUSALS. Any one of them keeps today's head. "Summed award" means a lot's latest award by notice id, as LotSums builds it today.

R1, a lot won by two or more separate tenders (Bm_g).
- Refuse when a summed lot's result names 2 or more winners and they are not all tenderers of ONE LotTender for that lot in the same round.
- A consortium on one LotTender counts as one tender.
- A TED award block with AWARDED_TO_GROUP also counts as one tender, even with no LotTender rows.
- No LotTender rows for the lot, 2 or more winners and no group flag: refuse.
- Fields: LotResultState.winners and Round.bids (lot_key, parties with role tenderer) are already there. ADD LotResultState.group from TED-AWARDED_TO_GROUP inside the award block. r209 already parses it as a Rule::Marker, so no re-parse is needed.

R2, published lot numbers (C_plus). Read each summed award's published lot number as a set of tokens: leading zeros dropped, ranges up to 50 expanded, lists split. Refuse when:
- (a) two summed keys share a token;
- (b) one award's lot number is a list of 2 or more;
- (c) one key's award rounds name different lot numbers;
- (d) the summed awards come from 2 or more notices and any of them has no lot number.
- Fields to ADD: LotResultState.published_lot_no and LotState.published_lot_no.
  - TED: the LOT_NO / LOT_NUMBER / ITEM value. project.rs's legacy results reader already reads it to resolve lot_key, and then drops it.
  - eForms: BT-13713 as published.
  - FTS: the OCDS lot id.
- Today the stored key is TED's ordinal LOT-k. R2 closes G8b's ordinal blind spot (the S3a–d shapes).

R3, a notice's total below the lots it awards (D_keys).
- Take each round notice that awards a summed key and has an award-type total in S's currency: BT-161-NoticeResult, TED VAL_TOTAL at notice or procedure scope, BT-118-NoticeResult or BT-1118-NoticeResult. A single-lot notice's total equal to its own award does not count.
- Refuse when the summed awards of the keys that notice awards exceed 1.01 × its largest such total.
- With no such total anywhere: refuse when S > 10 × the largest estimate in the chain (BT-27 at Lot or Procedure, VAL_ESTIMATED_TOTAL, framework maximum).
- Fields to ADD: TenderVersion.stated_totals, a list of {notice_id, field, cents, currency, lots the notice awards}, cumulative over the chain like rounds (or read from ScalePartners' chain-wide figures).
  - BT-118 and BT-1118 are parsed but unmapped. They are READ here only, never written as an amount row and never elected (506 stands).
  - Estimates are already there.

R4 (E): a summed award at least 10 × its own lot's largest BT-27-Lot.
- Already there for eForms and FTS lots.
- TED lot estimates are stored with no lot, so R4 never fires on TED. That gap is recorded, not fixed.

R5: the 15 shape checks from the shapes pass. All inputs are already there: rounds, LotState amount facts including the partner-only BT-709 / BT-660 rows (read, never summed), and bids.
1. The summed result's decision starts with "clos", or it has no winner.
2. A later result on the same lot is closed, or has neither a winner nor a value.
3. An award is within 0.5 % of the sum of all lot estimates (at least 2 lots carry one).
4. An award is within 0.5 % of the sum of every lot's figure in one other round, or in one kind (BT-27-Lot, BT-709, BT-660, BT-271-Lot), over at least 2 lots.
5. An award is above 1.01 × the sum of its own valued bids in that round.
6. An award is at least 1.9 × its lot's BT-709.
7. S is above 1.5 × the sum of BT-709 over the summed lots that carry one.
8. An award is at least 1.5 × its lot's smallest estimate.
9. An award is at least 3 × its lot's estimate.
10. S is above 3 × the sum of the estimates of the summed lots that carry one.
11. Two or more equal valued bids equal the lot's BT-709, BT-660, BT-27 or BT-271 (within 0.1 %).
12. An award equals n_winners × one of the lot's BT-709, BT-660, BT-27 or BT-271 (within 0.1 %), with n_winners at least 2.
13. S is below 1,000.00 in its own currency.
14. A procedure estimate equals every lot's estimate (within 0.1 %).
15. All lot estimates are equal (at least 2 lots carry one).

R6 (C_title): two summed keys, awarded in different notices, have the same non-empty winner set and the same normalised lot title. Already there (lot "title" facts).

R7 (P10): a summed award is at least 10 × or at most 1/10 of an earlier valued award on the same key, in the same currency. Already there (rounds).

R8 (DOM10): the largest summed award is at least 10 × the second largest. Already there.

R9 (new; it refuses 27915 and 8597433 and 0 rights): the summed result's round publishes LotTenders, but none for the summed lot. This is the shape where an award is resolved through another lot's contract or tender. Already there (Round.bids lot_key).

R10, the band vouch (new):
- When S_eur is EUR 100,000,000.00 or more, refuse unless some stated total T vouches for S:
  - T is in S's currency and comes from any notice in the chain;
  - |T − S| ≤ 1 % of S;
  - T equals no single summed award, and is not a single-lot notice's own award.
- Kinds accepted: BT-161, TED VAL_TOTAL, BT-118, BT-1118, BT-27-Procedure, TED VAL_ESTIMATED_TOTAL, TED VAL_RANGE_TOTAL LOW/HIGH. Modification VAL_TOTAL_BEFORE/AFTER do not count.
- Fields: the same stated_totals as R3 (ADD).
- The detail JSON gains `vouched_by {field, notice_id, cents}` whenever a vouching total exists, at any size.

NOT adopted:
- A, the framework/DPS flag: 33 more lost fixes, including 8426318 and 585917, to catch one band wrong that R9 already catches.
- B, "one contractor holds 2 or more lots": it hits 101 rights.
- Z / Z_nototal, "sum only where no total is stated": the evidence runs the other way (see the rationale).

PARSE: nothing new. Every fact above is already in the parse layer. The change is in the projection only (ingest project.rs feeding store's canonical types), kept in memory, with no new columns and no schema change.

judge.go_bar:
The bar is fixed and is not relaxed. Path W is switched on only when both of these hold:

(1) At most 1 wrong in a FRESH uniform 30 of v2's fires.
- None of the 30 may be among the 279 labelled ids.
- The salt is recorded in the issue before the draw.
- The draw is the shadow walk in M1, so nothing ships to make it. Walk the failed drain's 15,352 path-W corrections (project 2575, /v1/changes cursor 955146761 to 955254530) in salted order, score each id with the Python port of v2 on public-API facts, and keep the first 30 that v2 ships. v2 only adds refusals to v1, so this is a uniform draw of its fires.

(2) 0 heads labelled farther or double_count when every v2 head of EUR 100 m or more is read in full.
- That is the 15 band heads, re-read blind, plus any band head the walk finds that is not among them.

Both reads use wf_dc85fa7e-c00's rubric and put a skeptic on every wrong.

Order of tests, fixed in advance:
- v2 first.
- If v2 fails, "vouched everywhere" (R10 at every size) once, from the same walk.
- If that also fails, path W stays withdrawn (unit X).

Nothing in canonical.rs flips before (1) and (2) pass on the Python port. After B3, the Rust and the port must agree with 0 disagreements on every id walked or labelled.

After the drain, B5 repeats both checks on the real population: 30 drawn by a new salt, plus the band in full. A failure there switches path W off and refolds back by unit 4a's route.

Stop rules during the drain:
- Corrections outside 0.5x–2x of M1's projection: stop.
- A pin off: stop.
- A band set different from M2's: stop.
judge.rationale:
WHY REDESIGN RATHER THAN KEEP WITHDRAWN
- The failure sits in shapes we can name.
- The facts that separate them (TED LOT_NO, AWARDED_TO_GROUP, BT-118/BT-1118, per-notice totals) are already parsed. They are only dropped by the projection, so the build needs no re-parse.
- About 9,800 understated heads (1.5x–569x) are at stake.
- The test costs about 190 GETs and one panel read, and ships nothing. Measuring before building means a failure wastes no Rust work.
- This is still fail-closed: every new check only refuses, and a refused head keeps the max election.

WHY NOT THE SCORED W13 OR W12
- The EUR 100 m band is a fixed population: the redesign's band heads are a subset of the 229 already read.
- On it, W13 ships 27915 (a double count: LOT-0002's result resolves to LOT-0003's CON-0002/TEN-0002) and 51385 (two x1000 awards; its reader calls the sum farther). W12 ships 51385.
- So both would fail the band read deterministically.
- R9 (the round has LotTenders, but none for the summed lot) catches 27915 and costs 0 rights.
- R10 catches 51385 and every other band wrong by requiring a total the buyer stated. That is path V's principle at k = 0, and it is the positive signal the earlier units found: BT-118 confirmed the lot sum wherever unit 1 saw it.
- Measured on the labels, a sum that matches a stated total was right in 34 of 39 cases, and in 12 of 12 in the sample. The 4 such band wrongs (867196, 5561539, 6972400, 8259278) are all refused by R1–R9.
- v2 therefore ships 0 band wrongs of any class in-sample. It loses the Lyon-Turin trio and 8831876, whose totals are not in their own chain; failing closed means accepting that.

WHY NOT THE OTHER CANDIDATES
- A, the framework flag: costs 33 more fixes (including 8426318 and 585917) for one band wrong that R9 already catches.
- The owner's "sum only where no total is stated" (Z_nototal): the evidence runs the other way. It ships 3 wrong of 16 band heads and 1 of 7 sample heads, and only about 2,149 fires.
- B ("one contractor holds 2 or more lots"): it hits 101 rights.

WHAT IS STILL UNCERTAIN
- All results are in-sample. R5–R8 and Bm_g's consortium exception were chosen after reading leftover wrongs.
- In favour: each of the uniform sample's 9 wrongs is caught by a check with a stated reason (Bm_g; R5's closed-lot and below-1,000.00 checks; D_keys; C_plus).
- Estimated chance of passing the fresh 30: about 0.55–0.88 if 2–5 % of fires are wrong, and 0.15 at the in-sample upper bound of 11 %.
- The fallback, "vouched everywhere", is fixed in advance and tested once. Its about 2,450 fires rest on the buyer's own total, so it should pass more often.
- If both fail, the remaining wrongs trace to defects in the fold, not to the guards: TED's ordinal LOT-k keying, 492(c) collapsing stated totals into award copies, and x10^k award slips. Unit X files those.

FILES
- My scoring scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/d551w/judge/: common.py, j6.py, j7.py.
- They are built on d551w/score.py and px/features_all.json.
- v2 rows on the labels: band refused 96 wrong / 106 right / 12 neutral and shipped 14 right / 1 neutral; sample refused 9 wrong / 8 right / 1 neutral and shipped 32 right.

objections: B1 and the rule's R2 field text count TED-ITEM as a published lot number ('TED LOT_NO/LOT_NUMBER/ITEM in the award block'). That breaks the rule's own in-sample result. The r209 parser emits TED-ITEM from the ITEM attribute that every Section element carries (crates/ingest/src/r209/parse.rs:344): it is the block's position in document order, not a published lot number. So a single-section TED notice's award block reads as lot '1'. The Python scorer never used ITEM (extract.py files it as 'item'). Re-scoring v2 with ITEM as the fallback (adv/a5.py) ships 6421819, a sample wrong labelled farther. Only R2(d) refused it: LOT-1's notice 21205884 has ITEM 1 and no LOT_NO. The sample goes from 0/32 to 1 wrong in 33 ships, and M1's assert '105/105 wrongs refused' fails. 12 of the 279 hold a summed TED award with ITEM but no LOT_NO, 7 of them wrongs. This is the TED re-keying shape R2 exists to close.

B2 contradicts the rule. The rule keeps G8b unchanged, yet B2's R2 test says 'TED LOT-1 for lot 3 beside eForms LOT-0001 now sums'. G8b (canonical.rs names_one_lot_twice) refuses exactly that pair, because both keys spell 1. Making the test pass means weakening G8b. Then v2 is no longer v1 plus refusals: it fires on heads v1 never fired on. The 2575 correction set cannot sample those heads, so the walk's 'uniform draw of v2's fires' argument fails, and fails for the TED ordinal shapes (S3a–d) where double counts concentrate.

The walk cannot tell which ids are path-W fires, and the port as specified does not check. Unit 4a removed every lot-sum-awards row, and /v1/changes rows carry no derivation. So nothing confirms an id in cursor 955146761–955254530 was a v1 fire: the range may also hold path-V heads, incidental corrections or interleaved ingest. M1 builds rule_v2.py as 'the scorer's facts() plus R9 and R10' and checks only G0. facts() has no T', K, G1', G2, G3, G4, G5, G5', G6, G7, G8 or G8b, because all 279 were already served lot-sum-awards. A walked id with an admitted procedure figure (T' fails) or a repeated total (G1') could be 'shipped' by the port, read in M2 and counted as a v2 fire.

The bar leans toward passing. Both reads put a skeptic on every wrong but never on a right. The 279 labels were built the same way (108 first-read wrongs, 105 upheld; rights never challenged). A false 'right' is exactly the error that lets a bad rule pass '≤1 wrong of 30'. The band bar re-reads 15 heads already labelled right/neutral with the same rubric, which tests reader consistency, not correctness.

Band bar (2) bars only farther and double_count. not_additive (41 of 105 wrongs, the largest class and dominant among large heads), slip and other could all ship in the band and still pass. The judge's own case against W13 treats 51385, a slip, as disqualifying. And v2 ships 0 band wrongs of any class in-sample, so the narrower bar buys nothing in expectation.

Heads of EUR 10m–100m are effectively untested. The uniform 50 held 2 heads there, so a fresh 30 will hold about 1. v1's wrong rate rose with size: 18 % in the sample, 42 % in the band. R10 starts at EUR 100m, so a few hundred visible heads between EUR 10m and 100m ride on R1–R9 alone, with no read aimed at them.

Overfitting, quantified. R10 is the only refuser of exactly 1 wrong (51385) and costs 60 band rights (W14 ships 74 band rights; v2 ships 14). The R5 checks were picked because each hit 0 rights on these labels. C_title, P10, DOM10, R9 and Bm_g's consortium exception were added after reading the leftover wrongs. 3 of the sample's 9 wrongs are sums under 1,000.00 (324582, 5779166, 6330626). Below the band, the in-sample 0/32 says little; only the fresh 30 measures it. The band is a fixed, fully read population, so it is not overfit in the usual sense, but its 'right' labels never had a skeptic.

Band membership needs the exact stored rate. The scorer used the label group as the band, while rule_v2.py and the Rust use S_eur at the head's date. 1062828 (CHF 93,401,086.97, band right) is in the band only if CHF/EUR at its head date is at most 0.934, so it sits within about 1 % of the threshold. A port using different rates fails M1's 'band ships exactly the 15' assert, or misclassifies walk ids.

The evidence the decision names lives in this session's /tmp scratchpad: d551w/score.py, px and px2 features_all.json, shapes_work/features.json, judge/common.py, j6.py, j7.py. That scratchpad is session-scoped. M1's asserts and B3's parity check cannot be reproduced once it is gone.

Smaller points:
- R5.4 says 'one other round' but the scorer includes the award's own round (no in-sample difference, checked).
- R10's estimate-kind vouches rest on 1 right (7001924). The one in-sample estimate-style match outside the rule's list (5561539, an old contract notice's VALUE) was farther.
- TED-VALUE / TED-VALUE_COST-only vouches were 0 right / 2 wrong (adv/a10.py), so the rule's narrower list is better than the port's, which is one more reason the port must be aligned to it.
